newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Friday, boosted by gains in U.S. Treasuries after a decline in producer prices.
"The market is looking very well-placed for the coming week," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the market was principally driven by the U.S. where core producer prices fell 0.3 percent in May, the fifth consecutive decline in the index.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond was up 1/8 at 94-3/8, while the par bond was up 5/8 at 70-3/8.
The U.S. 30-year long bond rallied 25/32 to 98.27/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
Although the mood was overwhelmingly positive, some traders warned that the historically low Argentine spreads could make the market vulnerable to a bout of profit-taking.
"One needs to be slightly cautious in case of profit-taking," said another trader.
